readiness.mainReason: No blocking rule fired. The decision is clear, the core recommendation rests on sourced and honestly caveated evidence and the sequenced pilot leaves only refinement, not a change to what the client should do.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: The month-three full-launch trigger of 5% on slide 10 sits below the 8% year-one target on slide 8.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: The client's total income (to size the 5,000 pounds against the grant shortfall) or evidence that the 5% trigger is deliberately calibrated would confirm the level. Neither is a blocker on the text as written.

strengths.point: The deck answers the client question first and states the decision plainly.
strengths.quote: Client E should launch a paid membership scheme, starting with a single tier in the autumn.

strengths.point: Key claims are tied to named sources.
strengths.quote: Project grants are 80% of Client E's income (2024 accounts) and each is single-year.

strengths.point: Assumptions and risks are stated honestly with a test built in.
strengths.quote: We assume the mailing list is accurate and that members-only events do not strain staff.

strengths.point: The first steps name an owner, a sequence and a measure.
strengths.quote: The Client E coordinator owns the launch.

findings.title: The month-three go trigger of 5% sits below the 8% year-one target and is measured on the most engaged contacts.
findings.principle: Decision Consistency: a go/no-go threshold must match the success target and the population it is measured on.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 8 sets the year-one target at 8% of the full mailing list. Slide 10 triggers the full launch when the soft launch to the most engaged 200 contacts clears 5%. The most engaged contacts should convert above the full-list average, so clearing only 5% among them is a weaker signal than 8%, yet it green-lights the full launch.

evidence.quote: If 8% of the mailing list joins at 45 pounds, that is about 5,000 pounds in year one.
Month three: full launch if the soft launch clears 5%.

findings.why: A full launch triggered on a soft-launch result that predicts missing the year-one target could commit staff time to a scheme that underperforms, and the client cannot see that risk from the current gate.
findings.reflect: If your best 200 contacts convert at only 5%, what does that imply for the full list at 8%, and should that still trigger a full launch.
findings.fix: Reconcile the go trigger with the year-one target. Set the soft-launch bar at a level that predicts the 8% full-list target given these are the most engaged contacts, or state why a lower bar is acceptable.

findings.title: The 8% conversion assumption is reassured against an event-attendance rate, which measures a different behavior than paying for membership.
findings.principle: Evidence Grounding: benchmark an assumption against the behavior it actually predicts.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 8 calls 8% conservative against the 32% attendance rate. Attending an event is not the same commitment as paying 45 pounds a year, so the attendance figure does not on its own make 8% conservative.

evidence.quote: The 8% assumption is conservative against the 32% attendance rate and is the main thing to test.

findings.why: If the client reads 8% as safely conservative it may under-plan for a shortfall, because attendance does not directly predict willingness to pay.
findings.reflect: What behavior in your data most closely resembles paying for membership, and does it support 8%.
findings.fix: Ground the 8% in a proxy closer to paid commitment (past paid tickets or donors) or keep it as an untested assumption without the attendance comparison.

comments.problem: The year-one figure of about 5,000 pounds is not sized against the income gap it is meant to close.
comments.why: Grants are 80% of income and two of five are not expected to renew, so the client cannot tell whether 5,000 pounds materially diversifies income.
comments.fix: State total income and the size of the expected grant shortfall so the membership target can be judged against it.

comments.problem: The members-only discount with local partners is listed as existing capacity.
comments.why: The discount depends on partner agreement, not only on Client E capacity, so it may not be deliverable at launch.
comments.fix: Confirm the partner discounts are agreed or mark them as pending.

questionsForLead: What is Client E's total annual income, so the year-one 5,000 pounds can be judged against the gap from the two grants not expected to renew.
Is the 5% soft-launch trigger deliberately set below the 8% year-one target, given the soft launch goes to the most engaged 200 contacts.
Have the local-partner discounts been agreed, or are they still to be arranged.

learningNote.lesson: A go/no-go gate is only useful when its threshold maps to your success target and the population it measures.
learningNote.weakHabit: Setting a checkpoint number without checking it against the target it is supposed to protect.
learningNote.exercise: For each gate in a plan, write the target it maps to and the group it is measured on, then confirm that passing the gate predicts hitting the target.

notAssessed: Client E's total annual income, so the materiality of 5,000 pounds could not be judged.
Whether the comparable non-profits are truly comparable in size and audience. Only their public prices were provided.
Visual design, layout and charts. Only slide text was provided.
Whether the two grants will in fact not renew. The deck cites funder letters not provided here.
